title: Securing AI Services with Managed Identity
description: Secure access to Azure AI services using managed identities instead of API keys.

data.text: API keys are the default way to authenticate to Azure AI services, but they have a major problem: if exposed, anyone can use them. Managed identities let your Azure resources (App Service, Functions, VMs) authenticate to AI services without storing any credentials.
How Managed Identity Works for AI Services

When you enable a managed identity on an App Service, it gets an identity in Azure AD. You then grant this identity a role (like Cognitive Services User) on the AI service. The app can now call the AI service using the managed identity token instead of an API key.

data.title: Benefits of Managed Identity for AI Services
items: No API keys to store, rotate, or protect in code
Azure AD handles authentication and authorization
Access can be audited through Azure AD sign-in logs
If the identity is compromised, revoke access instantly in Azure AD
Works with App Service, Functions, AKS, and VMs

data.title: Disable API Key Authentication
data.text: For production workloads, disable API key authentication on your AI services after enabling managed identity. In the Azure Portal, go to the Keys and Endpoint blade and select 'Disable' for local authentication.

terms.definition: An Azure SDK credential class that tries multiple authentication methods in order. It uses managed identity in Azure and falls back to local credentials (Azure CLI, Visual Studio) for development.
The RBAC role that grants read and query access to Azure AI services without exposing admin keys.
A setting on Azure AI resources that blocks API key and AAD user authentication, allowing only managed identity access.

data.title: Exercise: Migrate from API Key to Managed Identity
data.description: Replace API key authentication with managed identity in an existing app.
steps: Enable a system-assigned managed identity on your App Service
Create a role assignment granting Cognitive Services User role on your Azure OpenAI resource
Replace the API key authentication with DefaultAzureCredential
Test the app locally (uses Azure CLI credentials) and deployed (uses managed identity)
Disable local authentication on the Azure OpenAI resource
data.expectedOutcome: An app that authenticates to Azure AI services using managed identity, with no API keys in code.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Managed identities eliminate the need for API keys in your code
DefaultAzureCredential works locally and in Azure without code changes
Grant the minimum RBAC role needed for each AI service
Disable local authentication for production workloads
data.takeaway: Never hardcode AI service API keys in production. Managed identity is the secure, standard way to access Azure services.
